title: Confinement scaling as a linear algebra problem: the model that wins on cross-validation loses on a new machine
description:
An analysis of machine learning for tokamak energy confinement time on the real ITPA Global H-mode Confinement Database (HDB5, standard analysis set STD5). A random forest beats the published IPB98(y,2) scaling law by 41% in RMSLE under grouped cross-validation by discharge; under leave-one-tokamak-out the ordering of the fitted models reverses exactly, and the forest is worse than a log-linear power law on 13 of 13 held-out machines.

The failure is characterised three ways: error tracking Mahalanobis distance from the training data, the hard prediction bound of a tree ensemble, and a polynomial flexibility ladder showing that what flexibility costs is the tail of the error distribution rather than its centre. Ordering machines by size reproduces, inside the database, a size extrapolation matching the 1.82x jump from the database to ITER; at that cut the tree ensembles score closer to a constant predictor than to the power law.

A constrained hybrid (a power law plus a bounded, heavily damped correction on its log residuals) is then built and scored, and is the best blind model at the ITER-matched cut. Split-conformal intervals calibrated to 90% under cross-validation are shown to cover 35% of rows on an unseen machine and 3% across the ITER-matched cut at essentially unchanged width.

The repository contains the full pipeline, from-scratch least-squares solvers, all analysis scripts, the test suite, and the scripts that regenerate every reported number and figure. The HDB5 dataset itself is third-party data obtained from OSF and is not redistributed; it is pinned by SHA-256 and verified on load.
